title: OpenAI Model Spec updates how AI models should behave
summary: OpenAI updates Model Spec to define behavioral guidelines for AI models
detailed: OpenAI has updated its Model Spec, the public document outlining how its AI models should behave across products such as ChatGPT and its API platform.
OpenAI says models must understand what people are trying to achieve while considering the consequences of their actions.
The revised Spec offers clearer guidance on how models should use conversation history, memory and other contextual signals.
However, the updated Spec describes the behaviour OpenAI is working towards, not a standard every current model already meets.
sentences: OpenAI has updated its Model Spec, the public document outlining how its AI models should behave across products such as ChatGPT and its API platform.

Published on October 29, 2026, the revised document brings its guidance together under five core values: faithfulness to human intent, harm minimisation, honesty and transparency, human agency, and care.
The update comes as AI models take on increasingly complex tasks, where following a user's words literally may not always produce the right response.
OpenAI says models must understand what people are trying to achieve while considering the consequences of their actions.
The biggest change is a move away from a long list of behavioural rules towards a values-led framework.
OpenAI places faithfulness to human intent at its foundation.
Models should help users and developers achieve their goals while respecting safety and policy boundaries.
The remaining four values build on this principle.
Harm minimisation focuses on avoiding foreseeable risks and respecting firm safety limits.
Honesty and transparency require models to communicate what they know, acknowledge uncertainty and explain the actions they take.
Human agency focuses on helping people understand their options and make their own decisions.
Care asks models to consider everyone affected by their responses and respect relevant social and professional norms.
OpenAI also acknowledges that these values can sometimes conflict.
A model may need to weigh an immediate user instruction against privacy, safety or the potential impact on others.
The revised Spec offers clearer guidance on how models should use conversation history, memory and other contextual signals.
For instance, a model may draw on preferences a user has previously shared, but should make those assumptions visible and easy to correct.
It also updates the chain of command, which determines how models handle conflicting instructions.
Higher-priority directions, including OpenAI's safety rules, take precedence over developer and user requests.
The document further addresses human oversight, social norms and the need to communicate potential side effects of a model's actions.
OpenAI is also retiring much of the detailed style guidance found in earlier versions.
Instead, it wants models to adapt their communication to users' language, culture, preferences and context.
However, some defaults remain.
Models are expected to approach questions objectively rather than simply telling users what they want to hear.
Another change is the use of the term "GPT" instead of "the assistant", reflecting the models' use across different products and deployment settings.
The revised framework could influence how ChatGPT and other OpenAI-powered tools handle complex or sensitive requests.
Developers also get clearer guidance on the behavioural boundaries to consider when building applications with OpenAI models.
However, the updated Spec describes the behaviour OpenAI is working towards, not a standard every current model already meets.
The company says it will continue refining the document and its models through research, real-world use and feedback.
